title: High Pressure Protection
shortDescription: Refrigerant high-side pressure exceeded safe limit.
fullDescription:
E1 on Haier ACs indicates high-pressure protection has tripped. Causes include dirty condenser, blocked condenser fan, or overcharge.

Outdoor unit must cool before restart.

fixSteps.title: Clean coil
fixSteps.instruction: Wash outdoor condenser with gentle water spray.

fixSteps.title: Service call
fixSteps.instruction: If persistent, technician needed for refrigerant check.

title: Anti-Freeze Protection
fullDescription:
E2 means the indoor coil hit near-0C temperature, so compressor was stopped to prevent icing. Typical causes: dirty filter, low refrigerant, or low indoor fan speed.

Clean filter first.

fixSteps.title: Allow to thaw
fixSteps.instruction: Run in fan mode for 30 minutes.

title: Low Pressure Protection
shortDescription: Suction pressure too low - possible refrigerant leak.
fullDescription:
E3 indicates low-side pressure protection. Most commonly a slow refrigerant leak, but also possible with blocked line or stuck expansion valve.

Professional service required.
videoSearchQuery: Haier AC E3 low pressure leak

faq.a: Illegal and ineffective without finding the leak.

title: Compressor Discharge Overtemp
fullDescription:
E4 triggers when the compressor discharge thermistor sees excessive temperature. Can indicate low charge or failing compressor.

Service needed.

title: Overcurrent Protection
fullDescription:
E5 triggers when the compressor current exceeds safe limits. Common causes: low voltage, stuck compressor, or inverter module failure.

Verify supply voltage first; then service.

title: Communication Error
fullDescription:
E6 indicates loss of signal between indoor and outdoor units. Wiring or a failed inverter PCB are common causes.

Inspect interconnect cable first.

fixSteps.title: Inspect cable
fixSteps.instruction: Check continuity and terminal numbers match.

faq.a: Terminal block is inside outdoor unit cover.

title: Mode Conflict
fullDescription:
E7 indicates mode conflict on multi-zone systems - one indoor unit requested cool while another requested heat. Or a stuck mode memory.

Set all zones to the same mode.

fixSteps.title: Set uniform mode
fixSteps.instruction: All indoor units should share mode.

title: Indoor Fan Fault
shortDescription: Indoor blower motor not running at target.
fullDescription:
E8 indicates indoor fan speed feedback is abnormal. Causes: stalled blower wheel, bad motor or capacitor.

Power off, inspect blower wheel.

faq.a: Quiet unit, little to no airflow.

title: EEPROM Error
fullDescription:
E9 indicates the main control cannot read its configuration memory. Usually requires board replacement.

Power cycle first to rule out glitch.

title: Room Sensor Fault
fullDescription: F1 indicates a bad indoor room temperature sensor. Replacement is straightforward.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Open front panel and swap thermistor.

faq.a: Short term, but regulation will be off.

title: Indoor Coil Sensor Fault
fullDescription:
F2 indicates a faulty indoor coil sensor. Defrost and freeze protection depend on it.

Replace sensor.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Open front panel and swap coil sensor.

whenToCallPro: If the evaporator is iced up.

faq.a: Without coil sensor, freeze protection fails.

title: Outdoor Ambient Sensor Fault
fullDescription:
F3 indicates the outdoor ambient thermistor is out of range. Heat pump defrost logic relies on it.

Replace in outdoor unit.

faq.a: Probably, but heat-mode defrost may fail.

title: Outdoor Coil Sensor Fault
fullDescription:
F4 indicates the outdoor coil thermistor failure. Critical for heat-pump defrost.

Replace sensor clipped to outdoor coil.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new coil sensor on outdoor coil.

title: Outdoor Fan Fault
shortDescription: Condenser fan not running at target.
fullDescription:
F5 indicates outdoor fan motor feedback loss. Check debris, capacitor, motor.

Compressor protection will kick in.

title: IPM Protection
shortDescription: Inverter power module entered protection mode.
fullDescription:
F6 indicates Intelligent Power Module overcurrent/overtemperature. Possible causes: dirty coil, overheated module, failed IGBT.

Clean condenser first; if persistent, service.

faq.a: Often yes; whole outdoor unit replacement is sometimes comparable.

title: Haier E10 — Supply Voltage Out of Range
shortDescription: Haier Air Conditioner error E10: The unit detected mains voltage outside the safe operating range.
fullDescription: Error code E10 on Haier air conditioners indicates the unit detected mains voltage outside the safe operating range. This condition normally locks out cooling or heating until the fault is cleared. Common causes include a defective mains supply / voltage protection circuit, a loose or damaged wiring harness between the component and the main control board, or a failure of the control board itself. Begin with a hard power reset, then inspect the mains supply / voltage protection circuit and its wiring before considering board replacement.

causes.cause: Defective mains supply / voltage protection circuit

symptoms: E10 shown on the indoor display or remote
Compressor or fan does not start

fixSteps.title: Power reset
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the unit from power for 5 minutes, then restore power and observe whether the error returns.

fixSteps.title: Inspect wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Open the service panel and verify all connectors at the main control board are fully seated and undamaged.

fixSteps.title: Test the suspect component
fixSteps.instruction: Use a multimeter to verify resistance or continuity of the affected sensor or component, and compare against service manual specs.

fixSteps.title: Replace the failed part
fixSteps.instruction: Order the matching replacement part for your model, install it in the same orientation, and reconnect all wiring before re-testing.

whenToCallPro: If basic checks do not clear the E10 code, an HVAC technician should be called to verify refrigerant pressures and inverter operation.

faq.a: No — most units lock out operation when E10 is active. Resolve the fault before continued use.
